solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pulp song, with raw licks, 'Common People'

definitions.note: a plural-sounding phrase defining a collective noun phrase for ordinary folk

indicators.note: to pulp something is to mash it up, so the following letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A music critic describes the Pulp hit Common People as a song with raw guitar licks.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulp were a Britpop band whose 1995 hit Common People is about class, so 'Pulp' looks like the band name; it is the anagram signal on SONG plus RAW LICKS. 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Common people are the ordinary labouring section of society, the social group named by this phrase.

clue.text: Telegraph stringer?

parts.note: a stringer is a freelance newspaper correspondent, as the Telegraph might employ, but read literally it is someone who strings up telegraph lines

explanation.surface: A freelance reporter filing stories for the Telegraph newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes you think of this very newspaper and its freelance correspondents; the question mark warns that a telegraph is also the wire network, and a stringer is one who strings its cables.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who installs and maintains electrical or telegraph cables literally strings up telegraph lines.

clue.text: Kind of music opening creating harmony

parts.note: rap is a genre of music
a port is an opening, as a porthole or gun port in a ship's side

explanation.surface: A certain style of music starts off a performance and creates harmony among listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, sympathetic relationship, a social kind of harmony between people.

clue.text: Brains in cerebellum containing hollow

indicators.note: the words brains in cerebellum hold the answer within their letters, run across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A neurologist notes that part of the brain contains a hollow space.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from bRAINS through IN to CEREbellum. 'hollow' looks like a noun for a cavity, but it is an adjective meaning empty or false.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollow words or promises are empty and lack real feeling, the same as being false-hearted.

clue.text: Boss dropping right clanger

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall out of the boss word

parts.note: a gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A manager lets slip an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is everyday British slang for a boss; taking out R leaves the answer. A clanger is British for a blatant blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is British slang for an embarrassing mistake, a social blunder or faux pas.

clue.text: One found in pantry getting more overweight

indicators.note: found in places the numeral within the store-room word

parts.note: a larder is a pantry or food store
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A person discovered in the pantry is putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. The definition is a comparative adjective, matching the -IER ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardier is the comparative of lardy, British slang for fat, so it means fatter or heavier.

clue.text: A bird under good man showing energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the article and bird below the saint

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man
the mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A bird perches beneath a virtuous man, displaying vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under' means coming after, so the article and bird sit below the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the staying power or endurance that lets one sustain effort, a form of energy.

clue.text: Swift people?

parts.note: read not as fast runners but as people created by the satirist Jonathan Swift, the tiny islanders in Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A description of people who move quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the author Jonathan Swift, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny inhabitants of Lilliput in Gulliver's Travels are the best-known folk invented by Jonathan Swift.

clue.text: Breaks in rugby strip playing outside

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters go around the rugby abbreviation
playing suggests the letters of strip are put into play in a new order

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

explanation.surface: A rugby kit worn while playing outdoors gets damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' gives IRPTS; 'outside' wraps it round the rugby letters. 'Breaks in' looks like breaks inside, but it is the definition, a phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force one's way into a place suddenly, an invasion.

clue.text: Weapon's steady holding attention

indicators.note: holding says the steady word clasps the attention word inside it

parts.note: firm means steady or stable
to give someone your ear is to give them attention

explanation.surface: A weapon is held steadily, demanding attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a portable weapon that fires bullets.

clue.text: Temper's risen when mobile gives picture wrongly

indicators.note: mobile means moving around, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's temper flares when their mobile phone shows an inaccurate image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone but is the anagram signal; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent is to give a false or misleading account, painting an inaccurate portrait.

clue.text: Parody from weirdo about a politician

indicators.note: about says the weirdo word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a loon is a crazy or eccentric person
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A satirical piece produced by an oddball about a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a satirical piece ridiculing someone, a type of parody.

clue.text: Relic, it seems, contains extracts

indicators.note: contains says the answer is held within the run of the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: An archaeologist notes that an ancient relic appears to contain fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is rELIC IT Seems. 'extracts' looks like a plural noun, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response or information, the same as to extract it.

clue.text: Measure bottling old wine

indicators.note: bottling says the measure holds the abbreviation as if in a bottle

parts.note: a pint is a measure of liquid

explanation.surface: A measure of old wine is bottled.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a grape variety, and a wine made from it, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: 'Blame former wife? Blow me!', I scoffed

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
cor and blow me are both British exclamations of surprise
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: A man exclaims in surprise at being blamed by his ex-wife.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'blow me!'; 'scoffed' means ate greedily, not mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To excoriate is to criticise severely, a harsh form of censure.

clue.text: Check for cheats on public transport

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the cheats above the transport

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks, cheats
a train is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: An inspection to catch fare dodgers on buses and trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. In a down clue 'on' means placed on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrain or hold in check, limiting freedom of action.

clue.text: Club's managed by revolutionary in fashion

indicators.note: in says the managing and revolutionary pieces go inside the fashion word

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style
to run something is to manage it
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A nightclub run by a radical is very trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club's' is 'club is', the 's a link; 'by' joins two pieces. TON for fashion is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short thick stick carried as a weapon by police, a kind of cudgel.

clue.text: A French Democrat therefore will get to suffer

parts.note: UN is the French for a
ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A French politician has to endure hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get to' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo is to go through or experience something unpleasant, to endure it.

clue.text: Caught artist consuming crack, leading to disorder

indicators.note: consuming says the caught and artist letters swallow the crack word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
a crack or gap is a hole

explanation.surface: An artist arrested for taking crack cocaine ends up in a state of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' sets the crack between the cricket letter and the artist. 'leading to' is a link; 'crack' suggests the drug, but it means a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an infectious bowel illness, a medical disorder.

clue.text: One snaps segment preceding Queen

indicators.note: preceding says the segment comes before the queen

parts.note: a bit is a segment or piece
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps part of a royal procession before the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A biter is something that bites, such as a dog that snaps at people.

clue.text: Boris possibly admitting Tory leader left city

indicators.note: admitting says the shuffled name lets in the Tory initial
possibly says Boris is one possible arrangement of the letters
leader picks the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson perhaps welcomes the Tory leader and departs the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the name to BRISO, and 'admitting' lets the Tory initial in after its fourth letter. Bristol is a city in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a major port city in the West of England.

clue.text: They hold existence is sacred, truly sacred initially

definitions.text: They hold existence is sacred, truly sacred

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of each clue word in turn

explanation.surface: Believers who maintain that existence is holy, truly holy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: its initial letters spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Theists believe in a god, who holds being and creation to be holy.

clue.text: A right pair's accepting University's tough

indicators.note: accepting says the pairs take in the university letter

parts.note: read as the plural pairs, duos
U is short for university; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A couple of students find their university course hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts U inside DUOS, after DU.
explanation.definitionFit: Arduous means hard and strenuous, needing great effort, so tough.

clue.text: 'Best boy' maybe in charge of sound?

parts.note: a son is perhaps a mother's best boy

explanation.surface: On a film set, the best boy is apparently responsible for the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: A best boy is a film crew role, which suggests the sound department; here it is a loving name for a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound or sound waves, an adjective of acoustics.

clue.text: Muscle runs around ends of clavicle

indicators.note: around says the runs word goes about the picked letters

parts.note: trips are short journeys, runs

indicators.note: ends of picks the first and last letters of clavicle

explanation.surface: An anatomist describes a muscle running around the tips of the collarbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of' takes C and E from clavicle, which go inside TRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Doctor fish, discharging last of milt

indicators.note: discharging says a letter is let go from the fish

parts.note: the sturgeon is a large fish, famous for caviar

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of milt

explanation.surface: A fish expert sheds the last of the roe from a sturgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Milt is fish sperm, apt to the fish surface; its last letter T is dropped from STURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Tart is a nuisance embracing mechanic

indicators.note: embracing says the clue words clasp the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A mechanic is pestered by an annoying flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run tARTIS A Nuisance. 'mechanic' in its old sense is a manual worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic in the older sense is a skilled manual worker, a craftsperson.

clue.text: Cameron's land reforms provoking fireworks

indicators.note: reforms says the letters are formed again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: David Cameron's land reforms prompt heated protests.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron was a British Prime Minister. 'reforms' is the anagram signal on all of CAMERONS LAND; 'provoking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman candles are tubular fireworks that shoot out balls of coloured fire.
